data.exact_reserve_text: Claims expense - previous year (Gross 15.5 GBP m). Absent the retrospective reinsurance arrangement, reserve strengthening was required on the older years (2021 and prior) within the International Liability portfolio.

prior_year_events.impact_description: Reserve strengthening was required on the older years (2021 and prior) within the International Liability portfolio, and on Professional Indemnity and Irish and Australian & NZ Liability accounts.

data.standardized_narrative: The syndicate experienced a gross reserve strengthening of GBP 15.5 million for prior underwriting years, representing 1.14% of opening gross claims outstanding. This strengthening was primarily driven by higher loss experience on Professional Indemnity and Irish and Australian & NZ Liability accounts for the 2021 and prior underwriting years. The report also notes the ongoing uncertainty regarding claims inflation, which could lead to increased claims reserves.
raw_causal_phrases: reserve strengthening was required on the older years (2021 and prior) within the International Liability portfolio
higher loss experience on Professional Indemnity and have required reserve strengthening on the Irish and Australian & NZ Liability accounts

inflation remains higher than expected over the coming years, and elevated for longer than expected, or the impact on claims inflation is significantly higher with would lead to increased claims reserves
data.data_quality_notes: The claims development triangle on page 21 does not show year-on-year changes in estimates, but rather the current estimate at each development point, making it unsuitable for direct calculation of prior year development. The 'Claims expense - previous year' from the Technical Provisions note (page 20) is used as the primary source for prior year development. The '2013 and prior' column in the claims development triangle was excluded as per instructions for aggregate columns.
